text:
alex: Captured a long nsys run while reproducing the KV-cache hotpath perf regression (seq=512, batch=8). I need to share the trace with the team but it has small customer prompt fragments — where do folks want these uploaded and how should I redact?

jordan: Upload to s3://redwood-perf-traces/eng-runtime/ for now. Use the "perf-traces" lifecycle bucket. If it's sensitive, also mirror to gs://redwood-perf-traces-private/ and tag it priv.

alex: Nice. Any recommended filename/naming convention? And concrete redact steps?

sam: Naming: perf-trace_<root_ts>_<model>_seq<seq>_b<batch>_<kv/on|off>_<short-kernel-hash>.gz
Example: perf-trace_1749006789_llama13b_seq512_b8_kvON_kA3f2.gz
Include a .meta alongside the trace with: model, seq, batch, node-type, nsys-opts, kernel-config-hash, job-id, and short summary.

maria: For redaction: the main things to remove are any request/response text fields, api keys, customer ids, and emails. The chrome/perfetto traces usually have a bunch of "args" fields — strip those.

alex: Can you paste commands? I used nsys and ended up with *.qdrep and a sqlite export.

sam: Sure — quick workflow (replace paths):
```
# profile and export
nsys profile -o /tmp/run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt python -m serve.main
nsys export --output /tmp/run.sqlite --format sqlite /tmp/run.qdrep
python tools/nsys_to_chrome.py /tmp/run.sqlite /tmp/chrome_trace.json
# redact prompt fields (delete any field that looks like request/prompt/text)
cat /tmp/chrome_trace.json | jq '(.traceEvents[]) |= (del(.args.request, .args.prompt, .args.text, .args.raw))' > /tmp/trace_redacted.json
# quick grep to ensure we removed common secrets
grep -E "(api_key|customer_id|@|\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b)" /tmp/trace_redacted.json || echo "no obvious PII found"
# gzip for upload
gzip -9 -c /tmp/trace_redacted.json > perf-trace_1749006789_llama13b_seq512_b8_kvON_kA3f2.json.gz
```
Note: adjust jq filter depending on how your exporter names args.

jordan: If you want Perfetto UI links, convert to perfetto/generic trace format. We use the perfetto cloud viewer for quick annotation: https://perfetto.redwood.internal/upload (private). Upload the .json.gz and add tags in the UI (model, seq, kernel-hash).

maria: Important: do NOT include any full prompt examples in metadata either. Metadata should be short plain fields. If you need to show an example prompt, paste it into a separate ephemeral gist and mark as redacted/obf.

alex: Good call. Are there recommended kernel timeline annotations to add? I have nvtx ranges around kv-cache insert/lookups and the attention kernels.

sam: Yes - add NVTX ranges for: KV-LOOKUP, KV-INSERT, ATTENTION-FWD, ATTENTION-BACK, POSITIONAL-EMB. In Perfetto you can add custom track names. That makes hotspot spotting much faster. Also capture the kernel names and durations in the .meta file (top 5 kernels by time).

perf-bot: Friendly reminder — for any trace >100s or >2GB, please run `scripts/trace_shrink.py` to trim early/idle regions and to sample long-running kernels. Attach both full and trimmed if possible.

alex: Perfect, I'll scrub using the jq command, add the .meta, run the shrink script, upload to s3://redwood-perf-traces/eng-runtime/, and share the URL here with tags. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jordan: If you want a quick sanity check before upload ping me and I can scan for missed keys. Also add the job id so we can cross-reference logs.

alex: Will do. Uploading in ~15m.
